calls.summary:
# Experiment Details Re-design Sync
Date: 2026-10-06 | Duration: 44.40999984741211m

## Summary
The discussion covered an experiment redesign focused on simplifying configuration and preserving efficient workflows. The to-do list would move into a collapsible section with completion checkboxes and separate automatic and manual checks. Inline edits would be staged as drafts before publishing, with merge-conflict control during saving. Data sources would remain a tertiary element and appear conditionally when multiple sources exist, while selection could be locked to prevent invalid metric choices. Scheduling would be grouped with timing settings, including ramp-ups, and approval would be required before starting or deferring an experiment. New experiments would begin as drafts without a separate publish step, while duplicate drafts would generally be rejected. For the UI, vertical stacks were preferred for more than three variations, power-user inline editing would be retained, and metrics, overrides, filtering, and advanced settings would be grouped separately. Drafts should clarify configuration state, change requests should be separate objects for new and running experiments, and a separate discussion was needed for approvals and revisions.

## Keywords
approvals, redesign, draft management, scheduling, data source, variation layout

## Action Items
